subject: Dedicated footprint estimate — 8k vs 32k context, KV-cache scaling & int4/int8 tradeoffs for Atlas Health POC
messages:

Cc: Procurement <procure@atlashealth.ai>

Subject: Dedicated footprint for POC — context length & quantization questions

Hi Soojin,

Thanks again for the demo last week. Our infra team asked for a concrete GPU sizing for the POC so we can scope procurement. High-level asks:
- Target model variants: atlas-7b (default) and atlas-13b (optional); we want to evaluate both.
- Two context scenarios: short (8k) and long (32k).
- Expected concurrency: 30 active sessions during working hours, with spikes to 60 for short windows.
- Typical payload: multi-turn clinical summarization; average request generates ~900 tokens, peak ~1,800 tokens.
- Latency SLO: 300–400ms p95 for atlas-7b; atlas-13b can be relaxed to 700ms p95.
- Quantization options: we want tradeoffs for int8 and int4 (if supported).

Can you provide a recommended dedicated fleet footprint (GPU types and counts), memory per-GPU estimates accounting for KV-cache at both context lengths, and notes on throughput/latency tradeoffs? Also flag any fallbacks (e.g., smaller context or model variants) we should plan for.

We plan to include this estimate in procurement next week. Appreciate any attachment matrices.

Best,
Ellen
Head of Engineering
Atlas Health

Subject: Re: Dedicated footprint for POC — context length & quantization questions

Ellen — thanks for the clear requirements. Putting a concise estimate below; attached is a detailed sizing matrix (atlas_poc_sizing_matrix.xlsx) with per-GPU amortization and cost delta for reserved capacity. High-level summary:

1) Model memory baseline (approx, operational):
- atlas-7b (int8): ~6.5–8 GB weights on device when using our int8 kernel; FP16 would be ~13 GB.
- atlas-13b (int8): ~12–14 GB weights; FP16 ~26 GB.

2) KV-cache memory (rough rule of thumb we use):
- KV storage scales linearly with context tokens and active sessions. For our runtime: ~0.00045 GB (0.45 MB) per token per session of KV (both key+value + overhead).
  - 8k context per session => ~3.6 GB/session in KV.
  - 32k context per session => ~14.4 GB/session in KV.

3) Active sets & aggregation:
- Typical working concurrency 30 sessions:
  - atlas-7b, 8k: KV = 30 * 3.6 GB = 108 GB (shared across GPUs via partitioning/replication; see fleet choices below).
  - atlas-7b, 32k: KV = 30 * 14.4 GB = 432 GB.
- Peak concurrency 60 would double these numbers.

4) GPU memory needed per device (example pod configs):
- Small pod (single H100-80GB):
  - atlas-7b int8 + 8k KV for ~4 concurrent sessions colocated: weights 7.5 GB + KV per-device ~14 GB => comfortably fits on 80 GB with room for batch buffers and CUDA overhead.
  - atlas-7b 32k quickly exhausts KV for >1–2 sessions on one GPU.
- Medium cluster (8x H100-80GB nodes with sharded KV): good for 30 concurrent 8k sessions; for 32k contexts we'd recommend both larger cluster and KV-specialized nodes (see recommendation).

5) Quantization impact (int8 vs int4):
- int8: good balance — weights roughly half of FP16 in memory footprint with solid kernel support; slight latency improvement vs FP16 for our kernels.
- int4: memory drops ~2x vs int8 on weights, but runtime is still experimental for some ops; int4 reduces weight memory but KV/cache and activations still dominate for long contexts. Use int4 for atlas-7b 8k to lower GPU count; avoid int4 as the only lever for 32k workloads without more validation.

6) Recommended fleet (POC -> Dedicated reserved):
- Option A (cost-conscious, faster setup): 8 x A100-80GB (or cloud-equivalent) as a shared cluster for atlas-7b 8k workloads, sharded KV store across nodes + 2x smaller KV cache nodes for replication. This supports ~30 steady concurrency at 8k with headroom; for spikes we rely on burst policy to preemptible nodes.
- Option B (performance-first): 6 x H100-80GB with NVLink for KV-partitioning and lower tail latency; add 3 dedicated memory-optimized instances (CPU+RAM-heavy) to hold cold KV shards and serve prefix caching. This is the recommendation if Atlas wants consistent p95.
- For 32k: regardless of option, plan an additional KV-scaling layer — either NVMe-backed shard nodes + more GPUs or move to model-splitting (chunked attention) with reduced per-session concurrency. We estimate a minimum of 18 H100-80GB-equivalent GPUs to hit 30 steady 32k sessions with acceptable p95.

7) Fallbacks / rollout plan:
- Canary with atlas-7b int8 + 8k only to validate throughput.
- If latency or cost unacceptable for 32k, use dynamic truncation to 8k with client-side UX warning, or use atlas-13b with aggressive quantization but lower concurrency.

Next steps: Marissa will follow with firmware/kernel notes for int4 readiness and a per-GPU amortization table for reserved pricing. If procurement wants we can convert Option A/B into an offer with monthly committed nodes and an SLA.

I'll loop Vivek to confirm operational constraints (autoscale/burst policy).

Cheers,
Soojin Lee
Senior Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference

Ellen / team — adding technical caveats and a short checklist for procurement. Quick TL;DR: int8 is safe for both models; int4 gives good weight reduction but doesn't change KV memory, so its benefit is largest for weight-dominated setups (e.g., atlas-13b on smaller GPUs). Detailed points: 

- KV cache anatomy: keys+values + indexing overhead + per-session metadata. Our empirical measurements across customer workloads show 0.40–0.55 MB per token; I used 0.45 MB in Soojin's calc. That overhead comes from alignment, replication, and per-layer kv meta.
- Network considerations: sharded KV across GPUs needs 100 Gbps+ interconnect for stable p95 on long contexts — recommend Mellanox HDR or equivalent in private deployments.
- Disk-backed cold-KV: for infrequent segments we can spill to NVMe but that adds ~20–80ms penalty per spill; acceptable if customers can tolerate occasional higher tail latency.
- Quantization readiness: our int4 kernels are GA for 7B but still on opt-in for 13B; we'll provide a compatibility matrix in the redwood-quantization-notes.pdf included.

Procurement checklist (attach to RFP):
1) Target GPU SKU (A100-80GB or H100-80GB) and count by option.
2) Network fabric spec (100 Gbps+, RDMA recommended).
3) NVMe tier for cold-KV (recommended for 32k contexts).
4) Autoscale burst policy and preemptible node plan.
5) Support & SLA tier for dedicated capacity.

I'll prepare the finalized doc for procurement with amortized monthly pricing under Option A/B and a best-effort estimate for the 32k fully-resident case.

—Marissa
Director, Solutions Architecture
Redwood Inference
